Read deploy/k8s/regions/global-entry.Caddyfile: lines 9-22 match the lesson block character for character; 16 reverse_proxy donhang-north-control-plane:30090 donhang-south-control-plane:30090; 17 lb_policy {$LB_POLICY:first}; 18 health_uri /; 19 health_interval 2s; 20 health_timeout 1s.

reverse_proxy page: "`first` chooses the first available upstream, from the order they are defined in the config"; "`round_robin` iterates each upstream in turn". Page does not define "available"; that an upstream failing its check is not chosen is shown by execution: failover.txt prints south only after the pause, north again after unpause.

Round 2: claim now matches round-1 suggested_text. reverse_proxy page: "Active health checks perform health checking in the background on a timer." "To enable this, `health_uri` or `health_port` are required." health_timeout: "how long to wait for a reply before marking the backend as down". health_fails / health_passes: "Default: `1`." Lesson s3 "gets no calls until a later check passes" agrees.

Caddyfile Concepts > Environment variables: "Environment variables in this form are substituted before Caddyfile parsing begins"; "A default value can be specified for when the environment variable is not found, by using `:` as the delimiter between the variable name and the default value" (example {$DOMAIN:localhost}). Execution: LB_POLICY=round_robin gives 3 x north, 3 x south.

Docker bridge driver: "User-defined bridges provide automatic DNS resolution between containers." "On a user-defined bridge network, containers can resolve each other by name or alias." kind Known Issues: "KIND creates a separate docker network named `kind`". Execution: entry on --network kind reaching upstreams by name gets "greetings from donhang-north-control-plane".

Round 2: claim now matches round-1 suggested_text. docker container pause page: "The `docker pause` command suspends all processes in the specified containers." "On Linux, this uses the freezer cgroup." Lesson s4 "suspends every process in it, so nothing in north answers" stays within this.

Round 2: claim now says hang or fail and states the no-retry default for both policies. reverse_proxy page: "Retries are disabled by default."; http transport dial_timeout "Default: `3s`". failover.txt: "at least one call hung or failed before south answered: yes", then three south answers. Lesson s4 and the s6 active-active row now rest on this claim.

reverse_proxy page: health_passes "is the number of consecutive health checks required before marking the backend as healthy again. Default: `1`." plus `first` = first available upstream in config order. failover.sh 68 waits until a call returns north; failover.txt lines 21-26: three north answers after unpause.

Read failover.sh: lines 38-62 match the lesson block character for character; 39 call() curl -s -m 3 ... || echo "failed"; 44 entry_up first; 31-37 docker create / docker cp / docker start / until curl; 53 show docker pause donhang-north-control-plane; 55-59 loop breaks on *south*, else failed+1; 60 prints yes/no. scripts/lib/regions.sh line 7: show() { echo "\$ $*"; "$@"; }.

echo-region.yaml (read in round 1): Deployment echo-region, namespace regions, caddy respond --body "greetings from {env.NODE_NAME}" (a fixed reply, nothing stored between calls), NODE_NAME from spec.nodeName; readinessProbe httpGet / 8080; Service NodePort, nodePort 30090. Round-2 addition "keeping no state between calls" follows from the static respond body.

Service page, type NodePort: "Each node proxies that port (the same port number on every Node) into your Service." Pod lifecycle, Readiness probe: "If the readiness probe returns a failed state, the EndpointSlice controller removes the Pod's IP address from the EndpointSlices of all Services that match the Pod."

kind Quick Start: "kind runs a local Kubernetes cluster by using Docker containers as 'nodes'." and node container example "kind-control-plane". scripts/lib/regions.sh: clusters donhang-$name (2, 20), docker exec "donhang-$1-control-plane" (29). failover.txt: docker pause donhang-north-control-plane echoes the container name.

Follows from the reverse_proxy page: checks run "in the background on a timer" every health_interval; health_timeout is "how long to wait for a reply before marking the backend as down"; health_fails "Default: `1`". Worst case after a pass: up to one interval to the next check plus one timeout = about 2 s + 1 s here; 30s interval -> about 31 s. Stated as "roughly" in s9.

Round 2: "teams often" removed (s11 now "a team can"); opinion with its condition. "This Caddyfile cannot hold north back" follows from claim 4 (health_passes default 1, not set in the file) and claim 9.

Opinion following from claims 3 and 8 (the surviving region receives every call once the other is marked down; round_robin sends any call to either region), stated as a sizing consequence with its condition (stateless Pods).

Opinion following from claim 3: with first the second region receives no calls while the first passes its check, so a fault only it has is exercised only at failover; with round_robin both receive calls daily.
Recommendations in s7 each carry their condition (flapping region; stateless Pods and idle cost dominate; single-writer data), derived from claims 16-18.

Round 2: s5 now reads "A real setup can spread the entry itself over several sites, for example with DNS"; no prevalence left. Single point of failure follows from failover.sh line 33 (one container).
